research.title: Research
research.lead: Every island kept its records differently, so where you start depends on where your family came from. Pick an island, or if you’re new to this, start with the five steps.

sections.heading: Research by island
sections.html: Each guide covers the key records, the archives, what you can search online, and the surnames members are researching there. Each has a “Where should I look?” tool: tell it who you’re looking for and roughly when, and it suggests the records to try first.

sections.heading: Surnames we’re researching

sections.heading: Stuck? Ask us
sections.html:
Between us we cover Jamaica, the other islands and military records. Tell us who you’re looking for and what you’ve tried so far, and we’ll pass your question to the person best placed to help. Email us ({email}). We’re all volunteers, so a reply can take a little while.

At Solihull Core Library you can use FamilySearch and Ancestry for free, and see records for some islands that aren’t online at home. Come to a meeting and we’ll show you.

who-we-are.title: Who we are
who-we-are.lead: Volunteers helping people trace their Caribbean families, in Solihull and online, since 2008. We love family history, and we’re here to help you find yours.

sections.heading: Our story so far
sections.html:
Some of our founder members are still on the committee today. Newer members have joined them, so between us we have a wide range of experience in researching ancestors across the Caribbean.

  1. 2008

    The group begins

    Courses in Caribbean family history are made from a ten-week British beginners’ class, reshaped for people with Caribbean heritage.

  2. 2010

    Working with WAWI

    We start working alongside the WAWI Project (Why Are West Indians in this Country). Together we host the Windrush Dinner and Dance every June.

  3. 2011

    Records at the library

    At our request, Solihull Libraries become a FamilySearch affiliate. Every Solihull library now gives free access to FamilySearch’s digitised records.

  4. 2021

    Records unlocked

    Our Barbados group finds that registers they need on FamilySearch are locked, and asks for them to be opened. They can now be viewed anywhere in the world.

  5. 2022

    Our first open day

    A Black History Month exhibition and open day at Solihull Library, on tracing ancestors from the period of slavery.

  6. 2023

    75 years of Windrush

    A free exhibition at Solihull Library through October, honouring the Windrush generation.

  7. 2025

    A visit from the Mayor

    The Mayor of Solihull visits our Black History Month exhibition and open day.

sections.heading: Our aim is to make Caribbean family history open to everyone.
sections.html: That’s why our exhibitions and open days are free, why your first meeting is free, and why we meet on Zoom as well as in Solihull. Members now join us from across the UK, the USA, Jamaica and Trinidad.

sections.heading: What we do
sections.html:
• Monthly meetings

    On the last Saturday of the month, at Solihull Core Library and on Zoom. Bring a name, a photograph or a question.

  • Island research groups

    Members-only groups for Jamaica, Barbados, and St Kitts and Nevis with Anguilla, working through the records together.

  • Exhibitions and open days

    Free exhibitions for Black History Month and Windrush, with open days where anyone can ask about their family.

  • Help with your research

    Tell us who you’re looking for and what you’ve tried. We’ll pass your question to the member who knows that island or record best.

sections.heading: Where we meet
sections.html: Solihull Core Library is an Associate Family History Centre. Inside you can use almost all of FamilySearch’s online Caribbean records. At home, what you can see depends on the island: Jamaica and Barbados are almost fully open.

join.title: Join the group
join.lead: Come to a meeting first and see if we’re for you. If you like it, membership is £20 a year, and every meeting after that is free.

sections.heading: How to join
sections.html:
1. Come along for free

    Your first visit is free, at Solihull Core Library or on Zoom. Bring a name, a photograph or a question, and see if we’re for you.

  2. Join online

    Membership is £20 a year, paid through the Parish Chest. Or email us and we’ll tell you other ways to pay.

  3. Start researching with us

    We’ll send you the Zoom links, add you to the island research groups you’d like to join, and put your surnames on our list.

sections.heading: What you get
sections.html:
• Every meeting, free

    Members come to all our monthly meetings at no charge, in Solihull or on Zoom. Visitors pay £5 after their first time.

  • Island research groups

    Members-only groups for Jamaica, Barbados, and St Kitts and Nevis with Anguilla, working through the records together.

  • Your surnames on our list

    We add the names you’re researching, and put you in touch with anyone researching the same families.

  • Help from people who’ve done it

    Some of us have been researching for more than forty years. Bring the record you’re stuck on and someone will usually know where to look next.

sections.heading: Want to get more involved?
sections.html: Our AGM is held every May, and committee roles open up each year. Members also help at our exhibitions and open days, and some give talks about their own research.

sections.heading: Questions people ask
sections.html:
Do I need any experience?

No. Some of us started a few months ago. You don’t need a subscription either: a notebook, some patience and the people in your family who remember are enough to begin. Start with the five steps.

I don’t live near Solihull. Can I still join?

Yes. Every meeting is on Zoom as well as in the library, and members join us from across the UK, the USA, Jamaica and Trinidad.

Can I come before I decide?

Yes. Your first visit is free. After that it’s £5 a visit until you join.

How do I pay?

Online through the Parish Chest. If you’d rather pay another way, email us ({email}).

Who runs the group?

Volunteers. Our committee is elected at the AGM every May, and new people are always welcome to help.

join.intro: We’re a friendly group of volunteers. Some of us are experts in a particular island or in military records; some started a few months ago. Everyone is welcome.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lead: Whether you’re just starting out, stuck on a record, or want to come to a meeting, we’d love to hear from you.

sections.heading: Get in touch
sections.html:
• Email us

    {email}
    The quickest way to reach us. We’re all volunteers, so a reply can take a few days.

  • Come to a meeting

    The last Saturday of the month at Solihull Core Library, 2pm to 4pm, or on Zoom. Your first visit is free.

  • Ask a research question

    Tell us who you’re looking for and what you’ve tried. We’ll pass it to the member who knows that island or record best.

sections.heading: Asking about your research?
sections.html:
It helps to tell us:

  • Who you’re looking for: names, and other spellings you’ve seen.
  • Roughly when they were born, married or died.
  • Where: the island, and the parish or town if you know it.
  • What you’ve tried so far, so we don’t send you back to the same records.

You may also find your answer in our island guides: Jamaica, Barbados, St Kitts and Nevis, Trinidad and Tobago and other islands.

contact.intro: Send us a message below or email us directly. If it’s about your research, the more you can tell us, the better we can help.

privacy-and-cookies.title: Privacy and cookies
privacy-and-cookies.lead: How the Caribbean Family History Group looks after your personal data.

sections.html:
Introduction

The Caribbean Family History Group (CFHG) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data.

About CFHG

The Caribbean Family History Group (hereafter referred to as CFHG) promotes the study of Caribbean family history. We have monthly meetings, attend family history fairs and cultural events in the United Kingdom and also online. This document will give you information on how the CFHG collects and processes your personal data through your use of our website, including any data you may provide through the website or directly with us when you:

  • apply for membership
  • join our meetings
  • sign up to our newsletter
  • access any other services we provide

The data we collect about you

Personal data, or personal information, means any information about an individual from which that person can be identified.

We may collect, use, store and transfer different kinds of personal data about you as follows:

  • Identity Data includes title, first name, last name, username or similar identifier.
  • Contact Data includes address, email address and telephone number(s).
  • Financial Data –as a group we endeavour not to hold any financial details about you. If we do take any details to complete a transaction – this is destroyed or deleted as soon as the transaction is completed.
  • Transaction Data includes details about payments to and from you and other details of products and services you have purchased or received from us.
  • Technical Data may include internet protocol (IP) address, your login data, browser type and version, time zone setting and location, browser plug-in types and versions, operating system and platform and other technology on the devices you use to access our website.
  • Usage Data may include information about how you use our website.
  • Marketing and Communications Dataincludes your preferences in receiving marketing from us and your communication preferences.

How is your personal data collected?

We use different methods to collect data from and about you, including:

You may give us your contact details by filling in forms or by corresponding with us by post, phone, email or otherwise. This includes personal data you provide when you:

  • Apply for membership or any of our products or services;
  • Subscribe to our newsletter;
  • Provide us with historical information or submissions for our records or to assist you in a research query;
  • Give us some feedback;
  • Join us at a zoom meeting or face to face meeting. Photographs or recordings may be taken at these meetings. You have the option to turn off your camera and have/keep your name information anonymised at those times.

It is important that the personal data we hold about you is accurate and current. Please keep us informed if it changes during your relationship with us.

  • Automated technologies or interactions.As you interact with our website, we may automatically collect Technical Data about your equipment, browsing actions and patterns. We collect this personal data by using cookies, and other similar technologies.
  • Cookies.Our website uses small files called “Cookies” to improve your experience of the site and enable us to distinguish you from other users. The cookies we use are “analytical” cookies. They allow us to recognise and count the number of visitors and to see how visitors move around the site when they are using it. This will help us to improve the way our website works.
  • We may sometimes use video embedding, like YouTube (3rd party) to enhance your experience of content on our site.YouTube’s privacy notice including cookie policy is available at: https://policies.google.com/privacy?hl=en-GB&gl=uk
  • You can set your browser to refuse all or some browser cookies, or to alert you when websites set or access cookies.If you disable or refuse cookies, please note that some parts of our website may become inaccessible or not function properly.

Third-party links

Our website may include links to third-party websites, plug-ins and applications. Clicking on those links or enabling those connections may allow third parties to collect or share data about you. We do not control these third-party websites and are not responsible for their privacy statements. When you leave our website, we encourage you to read the privacy notice of every website you visit.

How we store your personal data

We do not have any physical premises and CFHG is operated by volunteers who may be working from home.

We will only use your personal data when the law allows us to, that is for legitimate requirements of operating a family history group.

We will only retain your personal data for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes we collected it for and including for the purposes of satisfying any legal, accounting, or reporting requirements.

Our volunteers will process your data using their home computer. Each volunteer only holds the data necessary for their needs,and for the length of time to process the task. The data may be transferred between volunteers using personal email. Paper records may be passed by hand or posted.

Data security & Process

We have put in place appropriate security measures to prevent your personal data from being accidentally lost, used or accessed in an unauthorised way. In addition, we limit access of your personal data to Core Committee members, and usually only to those officers for whom the data is part of their role. We have also put in place appropriate processes to be followed by the core committee.

Do we share your data?

We do not share your data with anyone outside the CFHG other than to:

  • Researchers outside of our organisation – in order to assist you with a research query. We will not disclose your contact details unless you give us permission to do so first.
  • Police, HMRC, other regulatory bodies where required by law.

How long will we use your personal data for?

We will only retain your personal data for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes we collected it for, including for the purposes of satisfying any legal, accounting, or reporting requirements. This period of time varies between the activities for which the data has been provided.

By law we must keep basic information about our members and customers (including Contact, Identity, Financial and Transaction Data) for six years after they cease being customers for tax purposes.

Opting out

You can ask us to stop sending you notification/marketing messages at any time by emailing us at: cfhg.sol.birm@gmail.com

Where you opt out of receiving these messages, this will not apply to any immediate removal of personal data provided to us as a result of, for example, your membership.

Your legal rights

Under certain circumstances, you have rights under data protection laws in relation to your personal data. These are the right to:

  • Request access to your personal data.This enables you to receive a copy of the personal data we hold about you and to check that we are lawfully processing it.
  • Request correction of your personal data.This enables you to have any incomplete or inaccurate data we hold about you corrected.
  • Request erasure of your personal data. This enables you to ask us to delete or remove personal data where there is no good reason for us continuing to retain and use it.
  • Withdraw consent – where we are relying on consent to process your personal data. However, this will not affect the lawfulness of any processing carried out before you withdraw your consent. If you withdraw your consent, we may not be able to provide certain products or services to you. We will advise you if this is the case at the time of your consent withdrawal.

If you wish to exercise any of the rights set out above, please contact us.

Concerns or Complaints

Should you at any time feel dissatisfied with how we have handled your personal data, you have the right to make a complaint to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), the UK supervisory authority for data protection issues ( *www.ico.org.uk* ). We would, however, appreciate the chance to deal with your concerns before you approach the ICO, so please contact us by email or in writing. Once the complaint is received it will be dealt with in the first instance by the Core Committee, the management team of the CFHG. We will endeavour to respond to and resolve all requests within one month. However, depending on the complexity, this may take longer.

Contact details

The Caribbean Family History Group

Postal address: c/o Core Library Solihull, Homer Road, Solihull, West Midlands B91 3RG, England.

Email address: cfhg.sol.birm@gmail.com

Telephone number: 0121 704 6934 / 07851 229235

Changes to the Privacy/GDPR Notice

We may need to update our Privacy/GDPR Notice from time to time. You can check it at any time on our website. We will alert members of any significant changes by email. The updated notice will be on our website.

This Privacy/GDPR notice is an ongoing document. If you feel there is any area of your privacy that has not been covered, do notify us.

Our website address is: http://caribbeanfamilyhistorygroup.org.

Version 1 – February 2021 Caribbean Family History Group

other-islands.lead: Our members research families right across the Caribbean, from Anguilla to Guyana. If your island doesn’t have a page of its own yet, start here.

sections.heading: Records that cover every island
sections.html:
• Slave registers, 1813 to 1834. Every British colony kept them. They are at The National Archives (series T 71) and can be searched on Ancestry.
  • Legacies of British Slavery. A free database of the owners and estates paid compensation when slavery ended. It helps you find where an enslaved ancestor lived.
  • Passenger lists to the UK, 1878 to 1960. Ships arriving in Britain listed every passenger, including the Windrush generation. They are at The National Archives (BT 26), on Ancestry and Findmypast.
  • FamilySearch. Free. Search by island to see which registers have been filmed and indexed.
  • Solihull Libraries’ island register. Lists when the state began registering births, marriages and deaths on each island, and what can be viewed at the library.
